title: Private Console: Degraded-Service Action Canvas & Rollback Flows
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: Operators running Private/VPC deployments need a clear, low-friction surface in the Redwood Console to quickly understand cluster degradation, run mitigation steps, and perform safe rollbacks. Existing status pages surface health but do not centralize actionable options (canary toggle, rollback, evasive routing, change rollback reasons) alongside recommended runbook steps. This ticket scopes a high-fidelity prototype for an 'Action Canvas' tied to degraded-service alerts that combines: incident context, suggested mitigation actions, quick rollback controls, and one-click links to audit logs and runbooks. Goals: reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM), lower cognitive load for on-call, and ensure rollbacks are auditable and reversible.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype screens for clustered action canvas with at least three mitigation actions (drain, canary toggle, rollback) in Figma
Design includes clear confirmation flows that surface potential customer impact and required approvals
Design handoff includes accessibility checks (keyboard focus order, color contrast, ARIA hints) and copy for audit log entries
Interaction spec for how canvas binds to an active incident and how it surfaces fallback model variants or regions
PM and Eng sign-off on feasibility and a clear list of implementation hooks (API events, telemetry points)
updates: 2026-03-05: Kickoff with PM and SRE — agreed scope includes rollback + canary toggle + incident timeline condensed into single canvas. SRE requested telemetry hooks for rollback reason and operator ID.
2026-03-06: Initial sketches — two patterns: (A) sidebar slide-over action canvas, (B) modal-first flow. Decided to prototype slide-over for non-disruptive investigation.

2026-03-07: Design critique with Eng — highlighted need for optimistic UI for rollback initiation and strong cancel/undo affordances. Eng requested explicit API contract for rollback (POST /clusters/:id/rollback) and suggested rate-limit guard UI.
2026-03-08: Figma prototype v0.1 completed — includes action cards, quick-runbook snippet, and compact incident timeline. Linked to mock audit-log entry template.
2026-03-09: PM review — requested copy edits to make rollback confirmations reference SLA tiers and to add a 'dry-run' option for canary changes. PM also requested telemetry event names.
2026-03-10: UX research session scheduled (03/12) to validate operator mental model; added acceptance criteria for keyboard-first flows and screen-reader announcements.
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: Inline runbook snippets reduce context switching but risk presenting stale ops guidance — mitigation: surface last-updated timestamp and link to canonical runbook.

Tradeoff: Exposing rollback controls in the UI increases accidental action risk — mitigation: implement multi-step confirmation with typed acknowledgement for P0 clusters and require SRE approval for customer-impacting rollbacks.
Scope decision: Exclude automated rollback heuristics from MVP; focus on human-in-the-loop controls and telemetry to enable a later ML-driven suggestion layer.
next_steps: Finalize Figma flows for slide-over canvas and mobile breakpoint
Create engineering handoff doc with event names, API shapes, and required telemetry (rollback.start, rollback.confirm, rollback.cancel)
Run 3 operator usability sessions (03/12—03/14) and iterate on copy and confirmation wording
Coordinate with SRE to define RBAC gating for rollback actions in Private deployments
